50/* Translate center to given coordinates (x,y). */
51class translation_3x3matrix : public matrix3x3<coord_t>
52{
53public:
54 /* Initialize translation to CENTER. */
55 translation_3x3matrix (point_t center)
56 {
57 (*this)(0, 2) = center.x;
58 (*this)(1, 2) = center.y;
59 }
60};
61
62/* Rotate by given angle. */
63class rotation_3x3matrix : public matrix3x3<coord_t>
64{
65public:
66 /* Initialize rotation by ROTATION degrees. */
67 rotation_3x3matrix (coord_t rotation)
68 {
69 rotation *= (coord_t)M_PI / 180;
70 const coord_t s = std::sin (rotation);
71 const coord_t c = std::cos (rotation);
72 (*this)(0, 0) = c; (*this)(0, 1) = -s;
73 (*this)(1, 0) = s; (*this)(1, 1) = c;
74 (*this)(2, 2) = 1;
75 }
76};
77
78/* Rotate by given angle. */
79class scale_3x3matrix : public matrix3x3<coord_t>
80{
81public:
82 /* Initialize rotation by ROTATION degrees. */
83 scale_3x3matrix (coord_t scale)
84 {
85 (*this)(0, 0) = scale;
86 (*this)(1, 1) = scale;
87 }
88};

90/* Return contrast which is useful for registration. */
91luminosity_t
92get_positional_color_contrast (scr_type type, rgbdata c, bool robust)
93{
94 /* Robust mode is used to detect coordinates and screen type completely.
95 Here we insist on getting difference between all three chanels. */
96 if (robust)
97 {
98 return std::min ({my_fabs (c.red - c.green), my_fabs (c.red - c.blue),
99 my_fabs (c.blue - c.green)});
100 }
101 /* In Paget like screens any difference is good since each color
102 forms a grid.
103 For screen with strips we only determine one direction and that one
104 is also always good. */
105 if (paget_like_screen_p (type)
106 || screen_with_vertical_strips_p (type))
107 {
108 luminosity_t mmin = std::min ({c.red, c.green, c.blue});
109 luminosity_t mmax = std::max ({c.red, c.green, c.blue});
110 return mmax - mmin;
111 }
112 /* Dufaycolor has green and blue squares, red strips.
113 We need contrast between the squares to determine position in both
114 directions. */
115 if (dufay_like_screen_p (type))
116 {
117 if (type == Dufay)
118 ;
119 else if (type == DioptichromeB)
120 std::swap (c.red, c.green);
121 else if (type == ImprovedDioptichromeB || type == Omnicolore)
122 std::swap (c.red, c.blue);
123 else
124 abort ();
125 luminosity_t mmin = std::min (c.blue, c.green);
126 luminosity_t mmax = std::max (c.blue, c.green);
127 return mmax - mmin;
128 }
129 abort ();
130}

132/* Callback used for sharpening. Fetch data from buffer R at point P.
133 WIDTH and HEIGHT are dimensions of the buffer. */
134rgbdata
135getdata_helper (rgbdata *r, int_point_t p, int width, int height)
136{
137 if (colorscreen_checking)
138 assert (p.x >= 0 && p.x < width && p.y >= 0 && p.y < height);
139 return r[p.y * width + p.x];
140}
141
142/* Sign of angle used for mesh transform. Compute sign of triangle formed
143 by P1, P2 and P3. */
144static coord_t
145sign (point_t p1, point_t p2, point_t p3)
146{
147 return (p1.x - p3.x) * (p2.y - p3.y) - (p2.x - p3.x) * (p1.y - p3.y);
148}
149
150/* Intersect two vectors starting at [X1, Y1] with direction [DX1, DY1]
151 and [X2, Y2] with direction [DX2, DY2]. Store result in [A, B]. */
152void
153intersect_vectors (coord_t x1, coord_t y1, coord_t dx1, coord_t dy1,
154 coord_t x2, coord_t y2, coord_t dx2, coord_t dy2,
155 coord_t *a, coord_t *b)
156{
157 matrix2x2<coord_t> m (dx1, -dx2, dy1, -dy2);
158 m = m.invert ();
159 m.apply_to_vector (x2 - x1, y2 - y1, a, b);
160}

162/* Clamp value V to range [MIN, MAX]. */
163inline void
164to_range (coord_t &v, coord_t min, coord_t max)
165{
166#if 0
167 if (!(v >= min))
168 v = min;
169 if (!(v <= max))
170 v = max;
171#endif
172
173 v = std::clamp (v, min, max);
174}
175
176/* V is in range 0...1 expand it to MINV...MAXV.
177 Finetuning works well if values are generally kept
178 in range 0...1. */
179inline coord_t
180expand_range (coord_t v, coord_t minv, coord_t maxv)
181{
182 return minv + v * (maxv - minv);
183}
184
185/* V is in range MINV...MAXV shrink it to 0...1. */
186inline coord_t
187shrink_range (coord_t v, coord_t minv, coord_t maxv)
188{
189 return (v - minv) * ((coord_t)1 / (maxv - minv));
190}

192/* Solver used to find parameters of simulated scan (position of the grid,
193 color of individual patches, lens blur ...) to match given scan tile
194 (described tile and tile_pos) as well as possible.
195 It is possible to match either in BW or RGB and choose set of parameters
196 to optimize for. */
197class finetune_solver
198{
199public:
200 static constexpr const int max_tiles = 8;
201
202 /* Data we need for each tile. */
203 class tile_data
204 {
205 public:
206 std::shared_ptr<bitmap_2d> outliers;
207 /* Tile positions */
208 int txmin, tymin;
209
210 /* Tile colors collected from the scan for faster access.
211 Empty for BW mode. */
212 std::vector<rgbdata> color;
213 /* Sharpened tile. */
214 rgbdata *sharpened_color = nullptr;
215 /* Memory buffer for sharpened tile when it is not alias of color. */
216 std::vector<rgbdata> sharpened_color_buffer;
217 /* Black and white tile.
218 Empty for color mode. */
219 std::vector<luminosity_t> bw;
220 /* Tile position */
221 std::vector<point_t> pos;
222 /* If we do not finetune offsets, fix one. Usually 0,0. */
223 point_t fixed_offset = { -10, -10 }, fixed_emulsion_offset = { -10, -10 };
224 /* Screen merging emulsion and unblurred screen. */
225 std::unique_ptr<screen> merged_scr;
226 /* Blurred screen used to render simulated scan. */
227 std::unique_ptr<screen> scr;
228
229 tile_data () {}
230 tile_data (const tile_data &) = delete;
231 tile_data (tile_data &&) = default;
232 tile_data &operator= (const tile_data &) = delete;
233 tile_data &operator= (tile_data &&) = default;
234 ~tile_data () = default;
235
236 protected:
237 friend finetune_solver;
238
239 /* Remember last settings, so we do not recompute screens uselessly. */
240 rgbdata last_emulsion_intensities = { -1, -1, -1 };
241 point_t last_emulsion_offset = { -10, -10 };
242 int last_screen_revision = -1;
243 point_t last_simulated_offset = { -100, -100 };
244
245 /* Simulation of screen. */
246 std::vector<rgbdata> simulated_screen;
247 };
248 tile_data tiles[max_tiles];

320 /* Range of position adjustment. Dufay screen has squares about size of 0.5
321 screen coordinates. adjusting within -0.2 to 0.2 makes sure we do not
322 exchange green for blue. */

456 /* Return correction to the scr-to-img map for TILEID.
457 Values are in vector V. */
458 point_t
459 get_offset (coord_t *v, int tileid) const
460 {
461 if (!optimize_position)
462 return tiles[tileid].fixed_offset;
463 /* Increase search range when we guess coordinates completely. */
464 if (optimize_coordinates == 1)
465 {
466 luminosity_t range = 0.5;
467 return { v[2 * tileid] * range, v[2 * tileid + 1] * range};
468 }
469 /* Screens with two-dimensional structure needs two offsets. */
470 if (!screen_with_vertical_strips_p (type))
471 {
472 coord_t range = dufay_like_screen_p (type) ? dufay_range : paget_range;
473 return { v[2 * tileid] * range, v[2 * tileid + 1] * range };
474 }
475 /* Screens with one-dimensional structure needs just one. */
476 else
477 return { v[tileid] * strips_range, 0 };
478 }
479
480 /* Set correction to the scr-to-img-map OFF for TILEID.
481 Store values in vector V. */
482 void
483 set_offset (coord_t *v, int tileid, point_t off)
484 {
485 if (!optimize_position)
486 {
487 tiles[tileid].fixed_offset = off;
488 return;
489 }
490 if (!screen_with_vertical_strips_p (type))
491 {
492 coord_t range = dufay_like_screen_p (type) ? dufay_range : paget_range;
493 v[2 * tileid] = off.x / range;
494 v[2 * tileid + 1] = off.y / range;
495 }
496 else
497 v[tileid] = off.x / strips_range;
498 }
499
500 /* Return displacement between the image layer and emulsion for TILEID.
501 Values are in vector V. */
502 point_t
503 get_emulsion_offset (coord_t *v, int tileid)
504 {
505 if (!optimize_emulsion_offset)
506 return tiles[tileid].fixed_emulsion_offset;
507 if (!screen_with_vertical_strips_p (type))
508 {
509 coord_t range = dufay_like_screen_p (type) ? dufay_range : paget_range;
510 /* Reduce range if is not removable and can only be
511 adjusted by angle of scanner. On the other hand
512 increase the range for non-removable screens since there is
513 lesser change to make off-by-one error when we have color of the
514 patch. */
515 if (integrated_screen_p (type))
516 range /= 2;
517 else
518 range *= 2;
519 return { v[emulsion_offset_index + 2 * tileid] * range,
520 v[emulsion_offset_index + 2 * tileid + 1] * range };
521 }
522 else
523 return { v[emulsion_offset_index + tileid] * (strips_range * (coord_t)2), 0 };
524 }
525 /* Set displacement between the image layer and emulsion OFF for TILEID.
526 Store values in vector V. */
527 void
528 set_emulsion_offset (coord_t *v, int tileid, point_t off)
529 {
530 if (!optimize_emulsion_offset)
531 {
532 tiles[tileid].fixed_emulsion_offset = off;
533 return;
534 }
535 if (!screen_with_vertical_strips_p (type))
536 {
537 coord_t range = dufay_like_screen_p (type) ? dufay_range : paget_range;
538 /* Reduce range if is not removable and can only be
539 adjusted by angle of scanner. */
540 if (integrated_screen_p (type))
541 range /= 2;
542 else
543 range *= 2;
544 v[emulsion_offset_index + 2 * tileid] = off.x / range;
545 v[emulsion_offset_index + 2 * tileid + 1] = off.y / range;
546 }
547 else
548 v[emulsion_offset_index + tileid] = off.x / (2 * strips_range);
549 }
550
551 /* Return current emulsion blur radius from vector V. Value is in screen
552 size. This does not use pixel_blur since physical emulsion is not
553 dependent on scanner parameters. */
554 coord_t
555 get_emulsion_blur_radius (coord_t *v)
556 {
557 if (!optimize_emulsion_blur)
558 return fixed_emulsion_blur;
559 /* screen::max_blur_radius allows so large blurs that the resulting
560 process would be next to useless. Also the minimal blur is non-zero. */
561 return v[emulsion_blur_index] * (screen::max_blur_radius * (coord_t)0.2 - (coord_t)0.03)
562 + (coord_t)0.03;
563 }
564
565 /* Set current emulsion blur radius BLUR.
566 Store values in vector V. */
567 void
568 set_emulsion_blur_radius (coord_t *v, coord_t blur)
569 {
570 if (!optimize_emulsion_blur)
571 fixed_emulsion_blur = blur;
572 else
573 v[emulsion_blur_index]
574 = (blur - (coord_t)0.03) / (screen::max_blur_radius * (coord_t)0.2 - (coord_t)0.03);
575 }
576
577 /* Return pixel blur for value V. Do pixel blurs in the range 0.3 ...
578 screen::max_blur_radius / pixel_size. Value is in pixels, not screen size.
579 Scans are always bit blurred at pixel level, so 0.3 should be reasonable
580 minima. */
581 coord_t
582 pixel_blur (coord_t v)
583 {
584 return expand_range (v, (coord_t)0.3, screen::max_blur_radius / pixel_size);
585 }
586 /* Inverse of pixel_blur. */
587 coord_t
588 rev_pixel_blur (coord_t v)
589 {
590 return shrink_range (v, (coord_t)0.3, screen::max_blur_radius / pixel_size);
591 }
592
593 /* Return sigma of screen from vector V. */
594 coord_t
595 get_scanner_mtf_sigma (coord_t *v)
596 {
597 if (!optimize_scanner_mtf_sigma)
598 return render_sharpen_params.scanner_mtf.sigma;
599 return v[mtf_sigma_index];
600 }
601
602 /* Return blur radius of screen from vector V. */
603 coord_t
604 get_scanner_mtf_defocus (coord_t *v)
605 {
606 if (!optimize_scanner_mtf_defocus && !optimize_scanner_mtf_channel_defocus)
607 return render_sharpen_params.scanner_mtf.simulate_diffraction_p ()
608 ? render_sharpen_params.scanner_mtf.defocus
609 : render_sharpen_params.scanner_mtf.blur_diameter;
610 if (optimize_scanner_mtf_channel_defocus)
611 return (v[mtf_defocus_index] + v[mtf_defocus_index + 1]
612 + v[mtf_defocus_index + 2])
613 * ((coord_t)1 / (coord_t)3);
614 return v[mtf_defocus_index];
615 }
616 /* Return blur radius of screen for individual channels from vector V. */
617 rgbdata
618 get_scanner_mtf_channel_defocus (coord_t *v)
619 {
620 if (!optimize_scanner_mtf_defocus && !optimize_scanner_mtf_channel_defocus)
621 {
622 auto r = render_sharpen_params.scanner_mtf.simulate_diffraction_p ()
623 ? render_sharpen_params.scanner_mtf.defocus
624 : render_sharpen_params.scanner_mtf.blur_diameter;
625 return { (luminosity_t)r, (luminosity_t)r, (luminosity_t)r };
626 }
627 if (!optimize_scanner_mtf_channel_defocus)
628 {
629 luminosity_t b = v[mtf_defocus_index];
630 return { b, b, b };
631 }
632 return { (luminosity_t)v[mtf_defocus_index],
633 (luminosity_t)v[mtf_defocus_index + 1],
634 (luminosity_t)v[mtf_defocus_index + 2] };
635 }
636
637 /* Return blur radius of screen from vector V. */
638 coord_t
639 get_blur_radius (coord_t *v)
640 {
641 if (optimize_screen_channel_blurs)
642 return pixel_blur (
643 (v[screen_index] + v[screen_index + 1] + v[screen_index + 2])
644 * ((coord_t)1 / (coord_t)3));
645 if (!optimize_screen_blur)
646 return fixed_blur;
647 return pixel_blur (v[screen_index]);
648 }
649 /* Set blur radius BLUR.
650 Store values in vector V. */
651 void
652 set_blur_radius (coord_t *v, coord_t blur)
653 {
654 if (optimize_screen_channel_blurs)
655 abort ();
656 if (!optimize_screen_blur)
657 fixed_blur = blur;
658 else
659 v[screen_index] = rev_pixel_blur (blur);
660 return;
661 }
662
663 /* Same as get_blur_radius but when optimizing blurs of individual
664 channels from vector V. */
665 rgbdata
666 get_channel_blur_radius (coord_t *v)
667 {
668 if (!optimize_screen_blur && !optimize_screen_channel_blurs)
669 return { (luminosity_t)fixed_blur, (luminosity_t)fixed_blur,
670 (luminosity_t)fixed_blur };
671 if (!optimize_screen_channel_blurs)
672 {
673 coord_t b = pixel_blur (v[screen_index]);
674 return { (luminosity_t)b, (luminosity_t)b, (luminosity_t)b };
675 }
676 return { (luminosity_t)pixel_blur (v[screen_index]),
677 (luminosity_t)pixel_blur (v[screen_index + 1]),
678 (luminosity_t)pixel_blur (v[screen_index + 2]) };
679 }
680
681 /* Return red strip width from vector V. */
682 coord_t
683 get_red_strip_width (coord_t *v)
684 {
685 if (!optimize_strips)
686 return fixed_red_width;
687 return v[strips_index];
688 }
689 /* Return green strip width from vector V. */
690 coord_t
691 get_green_strip_width (coord_t *v)
692 {
693 if (!optimize_strips)
694 return fixed_green_width;
695 return v[strips_index + 1];
696 }
697 /* Set red strip width W.
698 Store values in vector V. */
699 void
700 set_red_strip_width (coord_t *v, coord_t w)
701 {
702 if (!optimize_strips)
703 fixed_red_width = w;
704 else
705 v[strips_index] = w;
706 }
707 /* Set green strip width W.
708 Store values in vector V. */
709 void
710 set_green_strip_width (coord_t *v, coord_t w)
711 {
712 if (!optimize_strips)
713 fixed_green_width = w;
714 else
715 v[strips_index + 1] = w;
716 }
717
718 /* Scale of coordinate system for V. */
719 coord_t
720 get_scale (coord_t *v) const
721 {
722 if (!optimize_coordinates)
723 return 1;
724 if (optimize_coordinates == 1)
725 return v[coordinate_index] * 0.3 + 1;
726 return (1 + v[coordinate_index]) * 0.5 * (max_scale - min_scale) + min_scale;
727 }
728
729 /* Rotation of coordinate system for V. */
730 coord_t
731 get_rotation (coord_t *v) const
732 {
733 if (!optimize_coordinates)
734 return 0;
735 if (optimize_coordinates == 1)
736 return v[coordinate_index + 1] * 25;
737 return (1 + v[coordinate_index + 1]) * 0.5 * (max_rotate - min_rotate) + min_rotate;
738 }
739
740 /* Get screen coordinates of a given pixel P of a given tile TILEID.
741 Values are in vector V. */
742 pure_attr point_t
743 get_pos (coord_t *v, int tileid, int_point_t p) const
744 {
745 if (optimize_coordinates == 2)
746 return transformation.apply ({(coord_t)p.x, (coord_t)p.y});
747 if (optimize_coordinates)
748 return transformation.apply (tiles[tileid].pos[p.y * twidth + p.x]);
749 return tiles[tileid].pos[p.y * twidth + p.x] + get_offset (v, tileid);
750 }
751
752 /* Return true if we consider outliers. */
753 bool
754 has_outliers ()
755 {
756 return noutliers;
757 }

931
932 /* Constrain values in vector V to reasonable range. */
933 void
934 constrain (coord_t *v)
935 {
936 if (optimize_coordinates)
937 {
938 to_range (v[coordinate_index], -1, 1);
939 to_range (v[coordinate_index + 1], -1, 1);
940 }
941 /* x and y adjustments. */
942 if (optimize_position)
943 {
944 /* Two dimensional screens has two coordinates. */
945 if (!screen_with_vertical_strips_p (type))
946 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
947 {
948 to_range (v[tileid * 2 + 0], -1, 1);
949 to_range (v[tileid * 2 + 1], -1, 1);
950 }
951 /* One dimensional screens just one. */
952 else
953 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
954 to_range (v[tileid], -1, 1);
955 }
956 if (optimize_emulsion_offset)
957 {
958 /* Two dimensional screens has two coordinates. */
959 if (!screen_with_vertical_strips_p (type))
960 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
961 {
962 to_range (v[emulsion_offset_index + 2 * tileid + 0], -1, 1);
963 to_range (v[emulsion_offset_index + 2 * tileid + 1], -1, 1);
964 }
965 /* One dimensional screens just one. */
966 else
967 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
968 to_range (v[emulsion_offset_index + tileid], -1, 1);
969 }
970 if (fog_index >= 0)
971 {
972 assert (!colorscreen_checking || optimize_fog);
973 to_range (v[fog_index + 0], (coord_t)-0.1 / (coord_t)fog_range.red, (coord_t)1);
974 to_range (v[fog_index + 1], (coord_t)-0.1 / (coord_t)fog_range.green, (coord_t)1);
975 to_range (v[fog_index + 2], (coord_t)-0.1 / (coord_t)fog_range.blue, (coord_t)1);
976 }
977 if (!tiles[0].bw.empty () && !least_squares && !data_collection)
978 {
979 /* If infrared channel is simulated, negative values may be possible
980 and it is kind of hard to constrain to reasonable bounds.
981 Still allow values somewhat out of range to account for possible
982 over-exposure or cropping */
983 if (!bw_is_simulated_infrared)
984 {
985 to_range (v[color_index + 0], (coord_t)-0.1, (coord_t)1.1);
986 to_range (v[color_index + 1], (coord_t)-0.1, (coord_t)1.1);
987 to_range (v[color_index + 2], (coord_t)-0.1, (coord_t)1.1);
988 }
989 }
990 if (sharpen_index >= 0)
991 {
992 to_range (v[sharpen_index], (coord_t)0, (coord_t)5); // radius
993 to_range (v[sharpen_index + 1], (coord_t)0, (coord_t)1000); // amount
994 }
995 if (optimize_emulsion_blur)
996 to_range (v[emulsion_blur_index], (coord_t)0, (coord_t)1);
997 if (optimize_emulsion_intensities)
998 for (int i = 0; i < n_tiles * 3 - 1; i++)
999 /* First 2 values are normalized and make only sense in range 0..1
1000 Rest of values are relative to the first two and may be large if
1001 first patch is dark. */
1002 to_range (v[emulsion_intensity_index + i], (coord_t)0, i < 3 ? (coord_t)1 : (coord_t)100);
1003 if (optimize_screen_blur)
1004 to_range (v[screen_index], (coord_t)0, (coord_t)1);
1005 if (optimize_scanner_mtf_sigma)
1006 to_range (v[mtf_sigma_index], (coord_t)0, (coord_t)20);
1007 if (optimize_scanner_mtf_defocus)
1008 to_range (v[mtf_defocus_index], (coord_t)0, (coord_t)20);
1009 if (optimize_scanner_mtf_channel_defocus)
1010 {
1011 to_range (v[mtf_defocus_index], (coord_t)0, (coord_t)20);
1012 to_range (v[mtf_defocus_index + 1], (coord_t)0, (coord_t)20);
1013 to_range (v[mtf_defocus_index + 2], (coord_t)0, (coord_t)20);
1014 }
1015 if (optimize_screen_channel_blurs)
1016 {
1017 /* Screen blur radius. */
1018 to_range (v[screen_index + 0], (coord_t)0, (coord_t)1);
1019 to_range (v[screen_index + 1], (coord_t)0, (coord_t)1);
1020 to_range (v[screen_index + 2], (coord_t)0, (coord_t)1);
1021 }
1022 if (optimize_strips)
1023 {
1024 /* strip widths. */
1025 if (type == Dufay)
1026 {
1027 /* Dufay screen is
1028 RR
1029 BG
1030
1031 Red strip width is more narrow in Dufay screens
1032 so overall coverage of colors is equal. */
1033 to_range (v[strips_index + 0], (coord_t)0.1, (coord_t)0.6);
1034 /* Green strip width approx 0.5 in Dufay screens. */
1035 to_range (v[strips_index + 1], (coord_t)0.3, (coord_t)0.7);
1036 }
1037 /* Dioptichrome screens come in various combinations
1038 and strip widths. */
1039 else if (dufay_like_screen_p (type))
1040 {
1041 to_range (v[strips_index + 0], (coord_t)0.1, (coord_t)0.7);
1042 to_range (v[strips_index + 1], (coord_t)0.1, (coord_t)0.7);
1043 }
1044 /* Widths of red, green and blue strip needs to sub to 1
1045 when we have screens with vertical strips.
1046 Constrain the to min width of 0.1.
1047
1048 TODO: Warner powrie screens seems to have 4 strips with
1049 green second tiny green strip between red and blue. */
1050 else if (screen_with_vertical_strips_p (type))
1051 {
1052 to_range (v[strips_index + 0], (coord_t)0.1, (coord_t)0.7);
1053 to_range (v[strips_index + 1], (coord_t)0.1, (coord_t)0.9 - v[strips_index + 0]);
1054 }
1055 else
1056 abort ();
1057 }
1058 }
1059
1060 /* Free data used by least squares solver. */
1061 void
1062 free_least_squares ()
1063 {
1064 gsl_work.reset ();
1065 gsl_X.reset ();
1066 gsl_y[0].reset ();
1067 gsl_y[1].reset ();
1068 gsl_y[2].reset ();
1069 gsl_c.reset ();
1070 gsl_cov.reset ();
1071 least_squares_initialized = false;
1072 }
1073
1074 /* Allocate least square solver. */
1075 void
1076 alloc_least_squares ()
1077 {
1078 int matrixw;
1079
1080 /* In color mode we produce 3 equations. In easiest case
1081
1082 ss is simulated screen (in screen colors after blur)
1083 red is screen's red color
1084 green is screen's green color
1085 blue is screen's blue color
1086
1087 ss.red * red.red + ss.green * green.red + ss.blue * blue.red =
1088 tile.red ss.green * red.green + ss.green * green.green + ss.blue *
1089 blue.green = tile.green ss.blue * red.blue + ss.blue * green.blue +
1090 ss.blue * blue.blue = tile.blue
1091
1092 So there are 3 independent equations with 3 variables (red.*, green.*,
1093 blue.*) each. Tile can be normalized or after fog applied. If we apply
1094 fog, then we need to compute RHS each time, otherwise RHS is invariant
1095 and computed once.
1096
1097 If fog is optimized we do:
1098
1099 ss.red * red.red + ss.green * green.red + ss.blue * blue.red +
1100 fog.red = tile.red ss.green * red.green + ss.green * green.green +
1101 ss.blue * blue.green + fog.green = tile.green ss.blue * red.blue +
1102 ss.blue * green.blue + ss.blue * blue.blue + fog.blue = tile.blue
1103
1104 In this case there are 3 independent equations with 4 variables. We also
1105 add
1106
1107 fog.red = 0;
1108 fog.green = 0;
1109 fog.blue = 0;
1110
1111 Now if infrared is simulated we first we use non-linear solver to guess
1112 mix_weights and fog. Image layer (simulated infrared) intensity is
1113 computed by:
1114
1115 c = tile.red * mix_weights.red + tile.green * mix_weights.green +
1116 tile.blue * mix_weights.blue
1117
1118 We know that screen colors should have all the same intensity when
1119 scalled by the formula above. So we have:
1120
1121 red.red * mix_weights.red + red.green * mix_weights.green + red.blue
1122 * mix_weights.blue = cst green.red * mix_weights.red + green.green *
1123 mix_weights.green + green.blue * mix_weights.blue = cst blue.red *
1124 mix_weights.red + blue.green * mix_weights.green + blue.blue *
1125 mix_weights.blue = cst
1126
1127 (We put cst=1.) Consequently:
1128
1129 red.blue = (cst - red.red * mix_weights.red - red.green *
1130 mix_weights.green) / mix_weights.blue green.blue = (cst - green.red *
1131 mix_weights.red - green.green * mix_weights.green) / mix_weights.blue
1132 blue.blue = (cst - blue.red * mix_weights.red - blue.green *
1133 mix_weights.green) / mix_weights.blue
1134
1135 We want to optimize:
1136
1137 ss.red * c * red.red + ss.green * c * green.red + ss.blue * c * blue.red
1138 = tile.red - fog.red ss.green * c * red.green + ss.green * c *
1139 green.green + ss.blue * c * blue.green = tile.green - fog.green ss.blue
1140 * c * red.blue + ss.green * c * green.blue + ss.blue * c * blue.blue =
1141 tile.blue - fog.blue
1142
1143 There are 6 unknowns: red.red, red.green, green.red, green.green,
1144 blue.red and blue.green. Variables red.blue/green.blue/blue.blue are
1145 substituted by the identity above. We no longer can treat individual
1146 channels by independent equations. */
1147
1148 if (!tiles[0].color.empty ())
1149 {
1150 if (!simulate_infrared)
1151 {
1152 matrixw = 3;
1153 if (fog_by_least_squares)
1154 matrixw++;
1155 }
1156 else
1157 {
1158 matrixw = 6;
1159 if (fog_by_least_squares)
1160 matrixw += 3;
1161 }
1162 }
1163 /* In BW mode we guess intensity. */
1164 else
1165 matrixw = 1;
1166 int matrixh = sample_points () + (fog_by_least_squares != 0);
1167 if (simulate_infrared)
1168 matrixh *= 3;
1169 gsl_work.reset (gsl_multifit_linear_alloc (matrixh, matrixw));
1170 gsl_X.reset (gsl_matrix_alloc (matrixh, matrixw));
1171 gsl_y[0].reset (gsl_vector_alloc (matrixh));
1172 least_squares_initialized = false;
1173 if (!tiles[0].color.empty () && !simulate_infrared)
1174 {
1175 gsl_y[1].reset (gsl_vector_alloc (matrixh));
1176 gsl_y[2].reset (gsl_vector_alloc (matrixh));
1177 }
1178 gsl_c.reset (gsl_vector_alloc (matrixw));
1179 gsl_cov.reset (gsl_matrix_alloc (matrixw, matrixw));
1180 }
1181
1182 /* Initialize least square solver using values in vector V.
1183 Only those values which do not change during optimization are computed.
1184 Rest is done later.
1185
1186 In most settings we do not use least squares here and base everything on
1187 data collection. */
1188 void
1189 init_least_squares (coord_t *v)
1190 {
1191 last_fog = { 0, 0, 0 };
1192
1193 /* In color we solve 3 independent equations for red, green and blue
1194 channel. Initialize RHS sides which are invariant. */
1195 if (!tiles[0].color.empty () && !simulate_infrared)
1196 {
1197 int e = 0;
1198
1199 /* RHS side of all equations should expect the tile's color. */
1200 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
1201 for (int y = border; y < theight - border; y++)
1202 for (int x = border; x < twidth - border; x++)
1203 if (!noutliers || !tiles[tileid].outliers->test_bit (x, y))
1204 {
1205 rgbdata d = fog_by_least_squares
1206 ? get_pixel_nofog (tileid, { x, y })
1207 : get_pixel (v, tileid, { x, y });
1208 gsl_vector_set (gsl_y[0].get (), e, d.red);
1209 gsl_vector_set (gsl_y[1].get (), e, d.green);
1210 gsl_vector_set (gsl_y[2].get (), e, d.blue);
1211 e++;
1212 }
1213 /* We want fog to be 0. */
1214 if (fog_by_least_squares)
1215 {
1216 gsl_vector_set (gsl_y[0].get (), e, 0);
1217 gsl_vector_set (gsl_y[1].get (), e, 0);
1218 gsl_vector_set (gsl_y[2].get (), e, 0);
1219 e++;
1220 }
1221 if (e != (int)gsl_y[0]->size)
1222 abort ();
1223 }
1224 /* In infrared simulation we set everything later. */
1225 else if (!tiles[0].color.empty () && simulate_infrared)
1226 ;
1227 /* In BW mode there is only one equation to compute. */
1228 else
1229 {
1230 int e = 0;
1231 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
1232 for (int y = border; y < theight - border; y++)
1233 for (int x = border; x < twidth - border; x++)
1234 if (!noutliers || !tiles[tileid].outliers->test_bit (x, y))
1235 {
1236 gsl_vector_set (gsl_y[0].get (), e,
1237 bw_get_pixel (tileid, { x, y })
1238 / (2 * maxgray));
1239 e++;
1240 }
1241 if (e != (int)gsl_y[0]->size)
1242 abort ();
1243 }
1244 least_squares_initialized = true;
1245 }
1246
1247 /* Used to set up optimization of tile TILEID
1248 with left corner (CUR_TXMIN, CUR_TYMIN) and screen-to-image map MAP.
1249 if BW is true, ignore color data. RENDER is used to fetch data. */
1250 bool
1251 init_tile (int tileid, int cur_txmin, int cur_tymin, bool bw,
1252 scr_to_img &map, render &render)
1253 {
1254 tiles[tileid].txmin = cur_txmin;
1255 tiles[tileid].tymin = cur_tymin;
1256 type = map.get_type ();
1257 if (!bw)
1258 tiles[tileid].color.resize (twidth * theight);
1259 else
1260 tiles[tileid].bw.resize (twidth * theight);
1261
1262 tiles[tileid].pos.resize (twidth * theight);
1263 if ((tiles[tileid].color.empty () && tiles[tileid].bw.empty ())
1264 || tiles[tileid].pos.empty ())
1265 return false;
1266 for (int y = 0; y < theight; y++)
1267 for (int x = 0; x < twidth; x++)
1268 {
1269 tiles[tileid].pos[y * twidth + x]
1270 = map.to_scr ({ cur_txmin + x + (coord_t)0.5, cur_tymin + y + (coord_t)0.5 });
1271 if (!tiles[tileid].color.empty ())
1272 tiles[tileid].color[y * twidth + x]
1273 = render.get_unadjusted_rgb_pixel (
1274 { x + cur_txmin, y + cur_tymin });
1275 if (!tiles[tileid].bw.empty ())
1276 tiles[tileid].bw[y * twidth + x] = render.get_unadjusted_data (
1277 { x + cur_txmin, y + cur_tymin });
1278 }
1279 return true;
1280 }
1281
1282 /* This is hack used for coordinate discovery experiment.
1283 We should avoid need to copy everything from main solver. */
1284 bool
1285 copy_tile (int tileid, finetune_solver &other)
1286 {
1287 tiles[tileid].txmin = other.tiles[tileid].txmin;
1288 tiles[tileid].tymin = other.tiles[tileid].tymin;
1289 type = other.type;
1290 tiles[tileid].pos = other.tiles[tileid].pos;
1291 tiles[tileid].color = other.tiles[tileid].color;
1292 tiles[tileid].bw = other.tiles[tileid].bw;
1293 return true;
1294 }
1295
1296 /* Init solver with FLAGS, BLUR_RADIUS, RED_STRIP_WIDTH, GREEN_STRIP_WIDTH.
1297 If SIM_INFRARED is true, simulate infrared channel.
1298 IS_TILE_SHARPENED indicates if tile is already sharpened.
1299 RESULTS are previous results if any. */
1300 void
1301 init (uint64_t flags, coord_t blur_radius, coord_t red_strip_width,
1302 coord_t green_strip_width, bool sim_infrared, bool is_tile_sharpened,
1303 const std::vector<finetune_result> *results)
1304 {
1305 bw_is_simulated_infrared = sim_infrared;
1306
1307 /* First decide on what to optimize. */
1308 tile_sharpened = is_tile_sharpened;
1309 if (flags & finetune_guess_coordinates)
1310 optimize_coordinates = 2;
1311 else if (flags & finetune_coordinates)
1312 optimize_coordinates = 1;
1313 else
1314 optimize_coordinates = 0;
1315 optimize_position = flags & finetune_position;
1316 optimize_coordinate1 = flags & finetune_coordinates;
1317 optimize_screen_blur = flags & finetune_screen_blur;
1318 optimize_scanner_mtf_sigma = flags & finetune_scanner_mtf_sigma;
1319 optimize_scanner_mtf_defocus = flags & finetune_scanner_mtf_defocus;
1320 optimize_scanner_mtf_channel_defocus
1321 = flags & finetune_scanner_mtf_channel_defocus;
1322 optimize_screen_channel_blurs = flags & finetune_screen_channel_blurs;
1323 optimize_emulsion_blur = flags & finetune_emulsion_blur;
1324 optimize_strips
1325 = (flags & finetune_strips) && screen_with_varying_strips_p (type);
1326 /* Strips needs to be optimized only for some screens, like Dufay, Joly or
1327 * Powrie. */
1328 if (!screen_with_varying_strips_p (type))
1329 optimize_strips = false;
1330 /* For one tile the effect of fog can always be simulated by adjusting the
1331 colors of screen. If multiple tiles (and colors) are sampled we can try
1332 to estimate it. */
1333 optimize_fog = (flags & finetune_fog) && !tiles[0].color.empty () /*&& n_tiles > 1*/;
1334 /* Colors can be determined either by data collection, least squares
1335 or using nonlinear solver. Data collection is fastest, but only works
1336 if threshold and blurs are meaningful. Second two should be equivalent
1337 with least squares being faster and more robust (avoiding local
1338 minima).
1339
1340 We later use at most one of least squares and data collection. Mode
1341 that does not make sense is turned off. */
1342 least_squares = !(flags & finetune_no_least_squares);
1343 data_collection = !(flags & finetune_no_data_collection);
1344 simulate_infrared = (flags & finetune_simulate_infrared) && !tiles[0].color.empty ();
1345 optimize_sharpening
1346 = (flags & finetune_sharpening) && !tiles[0].color.empty ();
1347 optimize_mix_weights = false;
1348 optimize_mix_dark = false;
1349 optimize_emulsion_offset = false;
1350 /* TODO; We probably can sharpen and normalize. */
1351 normalize = !(flags & finetune_no_normalize) && !optimize_sharpening
1352 && !tiles[0].color.empty ();
1353 /* Normalization turns every color of every pixel to have sum of 1.
1354 This simplifies the optimization since it effectively removes
1355 the image layer and we can more easily estimate screen position and
1356 blur. However this removal is not precise since it can not account for
1357 scan sharpness. It is not useful to optimize emulsion blur.
1358 */
1359 if (!tiles[0].color.empty () && normalize)
1360 optimize_emulsion_blur = false;
1361 /* In infrared simulation we try to estimate the image layer.
1362 We want to be extra precise, so do not use data collection.
1363 Emulsion blur so far really has only chance to work on areas of
1364 solid saturated color. */
1365 if (simulate_infrared)
1366 {
1367 data_collection = normalize = optimize_emulsion_blur = false;
1368 if (least_squares)
1369 optimize_mix_weights = optimize_mix_dark = true;
1370 }
1371 /* When finetuning emulsion blur, tune also offset carefully. */
1372 if (!tiles[0].color.empty () && optimize_emulsion_blur
1373 && (optimize_screen_blur || optimize_screen_channel_blurs
1374 || optimize_scanner_mtf_sigma || optimize_scanner_mtf_defocus
1375 || optimize_scanner_mtf_channel_defocus))
1376 {
1377 optimize_emulsion_intensities = true;
1378 optimize_emulsion_offset = true;
1379 data_collection = false;
1380 }
1381 else
1382 optimize_emulsion_intensities = optimize_emulsion_offset = false;
1383
1384 /* To optimize emulsion blur we can either assume that screen blur
1385 is already known and use it or try to simulate everything including
1386 intensities. */
1387 if (optimize_emulsion_blur && !optimize_emulsion_intensities)
1388 optimize_screen_blur = optimize_screen_channel_blurs
1389 = optimize_scanner_mtf_sigma = optimize_scanner_mtf_defocus
1390 = optimize_scanner_mtf_channel_defocus = false;
1391 /* When simulating infrared fog needs to be subtracted before applying
1392 mixing weights. This makes equations non-linear. */
1393 fog_by_least_squares
1394 = (optimize_fog && !normalize && least_squares) && !simulate_infrared;
1395 // fog_by_least_squares = 0;
1396
1397 /* Data collection is faster, so if available prefer it over least
1398 squares. */
1399 if (data_collection)
1400 least_squares = false;
1401
1402 /* Next determine values to optimize. */
1403
1404 n_values = 0;
1405 /* Position needs 1 or 2 values per tile depending on if screen
1406 is 2d or 1d. */
1407 if (optimize_position)
1408 n_values += (1 + !screen_with_vertical_strips_p (type)) * n_tiles;
1409
1410 if (optimize_coordinates)
1411 {
1412 coordinate_index = n_values;
1413 n_values += 2;
1414 }
1415 else
1416 coordinate_index = -1;
1417
1418 /* When optimizing sharpening, be ready for borders of the tile to not be
1419 right. Also allocate the memory buffer. */
1420 if (optimize_sharpening)
1421 {
1422 sharpen_index = n_values;
1423 border = 10;
1424 n_values += 2;
1425 for (int i = 0; i < n_tiles; i++)
1426 tiles[i].sharpened_color_buffer.resize (twidth * theight);
1427 /* Determine minimum meaningful sharpening radius. */
1428 min_nonone_clen = 0.3;
1429 }
1430 else
1431 {
1432 sharpen_index = -1;
1433 border = 0;
1434 for (int i = 0; i < n_tiles; i++)
1435 tiles[i].sharpened_color = tiles[i].color.data ();
1436 }
1437
1438 /* When not doing data collection or least squares, we need to optimize
1439 * colors. */
1440 if (!least_squares && !data_collection)
1441 {
1442 color_index = n_values;
1443 /* 3*3 values for color.
1444 3 intensities for B&W */
1445 if (!tiles[0].color.empty ())
1446 n_values += 9;
1447 else
1448 n_values += 3;
1449 }
1450 else
1451 color_index = -1;
1452
1453 /* Fog is RGB value. We can not determine it in BW, since it can not
1454 be separated from color. */
1455 if (optimize_fog && !fog_by_least_squares)
1456 {
1457 fog_index = n_values;
1458 n_values += 3;
1459 }
1460 else
1461 fog_index = -1;
1462
1463 /* If we do not use least squares, mixing weights are 2 values.
1464 Last value is complement of the other two since we optimize
1465 screen colors freely.
1466
1467 If we use least squares then we need all 3 values since screen
1468 colors are normalized to have sum of (1,1,1) so we save some
1469 variables. */
1470 if (optimize_mix_weights)
1471 {
1472 mix_weights_index = n_values;
1473 n_values += 2 + (least_squares != 0);
1474 }
1475 else
1476 mix_weights_index = -1;
1477
1478 if (optimize_mix_dark)
1479 {
1480 mix_dark_index = n_values;
1481 n_values++;
1482 }
1483 else
1484 mix_dark_index = -1;
1485
1486 /* Try to gues intensity of emulsion below each of primary colors.
1487 Used when trying to determine emulsion blur.
1488 This must be per-tile since every tile is assumed to have different
1489 color (but uniform in each tile). */
1490 if (optimize_emulsion_intensities)
1491 {
1492 emulsion_intensity_index = n_values;
1493 n_values += 3 * n_tiles - 1;
1494 }
1495 else
1496 emulsion_intensity_index = -1;
1497 if (optimize_emulsion_offset)
1498 {
1499 emulsion_offset_index = n_values;
1500 n_values += (1 + !screen_with_vertical_strips_p (type)) * n_tiles;
1501 }
1502 else
1503 emulsion_offset_index = -1;
1504 if (optimize_emulsion_blur)
1505 {
1506 emulsion_blur_index = n_values;
1507 n_values += 1;
1508 }
1509 else
1510 emulsion_blur_index = -1;
1511
1512 /* Screen index has different meanings depending on how well
1513 we want to estimate the blur. */
1514 if (optimize_screen_channel_blurs)
1515 {
1516 screen_index = n_values;
1517 optimize_screen_blur = false;
1518 n_values += 3;
1519 assert (!optimize_screen_blur);
1520 }
1521 else if (optimize_screen_blur)
1522 {
1523 screen_index = n_values;
1524 n_values++;
1525 }
1526 else
1527 screen_index = -1;
1528
1529 if (optimize_scanner_mtf_sigma)
1530 {
1531 mtf_sigma_index = n_values;
1532 n_values++;
1533 }
1534 if (optimize_scanner_mtf_channel_defocus)
1535 {
1536 mtf_defocus_index = n_values;
1537 optimize_scanner_mtf_defocus = false;
1538 n_values += 3;
1539 }
1540 else if (optimize_scanner_mtf_defocus)
1541 {
1542 mtf_defocus_index = n_values;
1543 n_values++;
1544 }
1545
1546 if (optimize_strips)
1547 {
1548 strips_index = n_values;
1549 n_values += 2;
1550 }
1551 else
1552 strips_index = -1;
1553
1554 /* We know number of values to optimize; allocate them and get initial
1555 values. */
1556 start.resize (n_values, 0);
1557 /* Poison values, so we know we initialized them all. */
1558 if (colorscreen_checking)
1559 {
1560 for (int i = 0; i < n_values; i++)
1561 start[i] = INT_MAX;
1562 for (int i = 0; i < n_values; i++)
1563 assert (start[i] == INT_MAX);
1564 }
1565
1566 /* Allocate also memory for all simulations. */
1567 original_scr = std::make_shared<screen> ();
1568 if (optimize_emulsion_blur)
1569 emulsion_scr = std::make_shared<screen> ();
1570 if (optimize_emulsion_intensities)
1571 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
1572 tiles[tileid].merged_scr = std::make_unique<screen> ();
1573 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
1574 tiles[tileid].scr = std::make_unique<screen> ();
1575
1576 /* Set up cached values. */
1577 screen_revision = 0;
1578 last_blur = { -1, -1, -1 };
1579 last_scanner_mtf_sigma = -1;
1580 last_scanner_mtf_defocus = { -1, -1, -1 };
1581 last_emulsion_blur = -1;
1582 last_width = -1;
1583 last_height = -1;
1584
1585 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
1586 {
1587 tiles[tileid].last_emulsion_intensities = { -1, -1, -1 };
1588 tiles[tileid].last_emulsion_offset = { -100, -100 };
1589 tiles[tileid].last_screen_revision = -1;
1590 tiles[tileid].last_simulated_offset = { -100, -100 };
1591 }
1592 last_fog = { 0, 0, 0 };
1593
1594 /* If we are not reusing older results, offset should be 0
1595 since we assume scr-to-img map to be meaningful. */
1596 if (!results)
1597 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
1598 {
1599 set_offset (start.data (), tileid, { 0, 0 });
1600 set_emulsion_offset (start.data (), tileid, { 0, 0 });
1601 }
1602 else
1603 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
1604 {
1605 set_offset (start.data (), tileid, (*results)[tileid].screen_coord_adjust);
1606 set_emulsion_offset (start.data (), tileid,
1607 (*results)[tileid].emulsion_coord_adjust);
1608 }
1609 if (optimize_coordinates)
1610 {
1611 if (optimize_coordinates == 2)
1612 /* scale = (min_scale + max_scale)/2 */
1613 start [coordinate_index] = 0;
1614 else
1615 /* scale = 1 */
1616 start [coordinate_index] = 0;
1617 /* rotation = (min_rotation + max_rotation)/2 */
1618 start [coordinate_index + 1] = 0;
1619 }
1620
1621 /* Always start from scratch with sharpening; otherwise the optimizer tends
1622 to pick up very large values. */
1623 if (sharpen_index >= 0)
1624 {
1625 start[sharpen_index] = 0;
1626 start[sharpen_index + 1] = 0;
1627 }
1628
1629 /* Start with color being red, green and blue. */
1630 if (color_index >= 0)
1631 {
1632 if (!tiles[0].color.empty ())
1633 {
1634 start[color_index] = finetune_solver::rgbscale;
1635 start[color_index + 1] = 0;
1636 start[color_index + 2] = 0;
1637
1638 start[color_index + 3] = 0;
1639 start[color_index + 4] = finetune_solver::rgbscale;
1640 start[color_index + 5] = 0;
1641
1642 start[color_index + 6] = 0;
1643 start[color_index + 7] = 0;
1644 start[color_index + 8] = finetune_solver::rgbscale;
1645 }
1646 else
1647 {
1648 start[color_index] = 0;
1649 start[color_index + 1] = 0;
1650 start[color_index + 2] = 0;
1651 }
1652 }
1653
1654 if (optimize_emulsion_intensities)
1655 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < 3 * n_tiles - 1; tileid++)
1656 start[emulsion_intensity_index + tileid] = (coord_t)1 / (coord_t)3;
1657 /* Starting from small blur seems to work better, since other parameters
1658 are then more relevant. Sane scanner lens blurs are close to Nyquist
1659 frequency. */
1660 if (optimize_emulsion_blur)
1661 {
1662 coord_t blur = (coord_t)0.03;
1663 if (results)
1664 {
1665 histogram hist;
1666 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
1667 hist.pre_account ((*results)[tileid].emulsion_blur_radius);
1668 hist.finalize_range (65535);
1669 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
1670 hist.account ((*results)[tileid].emulsion_blur_radius);
1671 hist.finalize ();
1672 blur = hist.find_avg ((coord_t)0.1);
1673 }
1674 set_emulsion_blur_radius (start.data (), blur);
1675 if (my_fabs (get_emulsion_blur_radius (start.data ()) - blur) > (coord_t)0.01)
1676 {
1677 printf ("Emulsion blur %f %f\n", get_emulsion_blur_radius (start.data ()),
1678 blur);
1679 abort ();
1680 }
1681 }
1682 /* Avoid valgrind warnings on undefined values. We will not really
1683 use the value, but we will read it to set up last value tracking */
1684 else
1685 set_emulsion_blur_radius (start.data (), -1);
1686 if (optimize_screen_channel_blurs)
1687 start[screen_index] = start[screen_index + 1] = start[screen_index + 2]
1688 = rev_pixel_blur ((coord_t)0.3);
1689 else
1690 {
1691 /* Optimizations seem to work better when it starts from small blur. */
1692 if (optimize_screen_blur && !results)
1693 {
1694 if (!(flags & finetune_use_screen_blur))
1695 blur_radius = (coord_t)0.3;
1696 }
1697 if (results)
1698 {
1699 histogram hist;
1700 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
1701 hist.pre_account ((*results)[tileid].screen_blur_radius);
1702 hist.finalize_range (65535);
1703 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
1704 hist.account ((*results)[tileid].screen_blur_radius);
1705 hist.finalize ();
1706 blur_radius = hist.find_avg ((coord_t)0.1);
1707 }
1708 set_blur_radius (start.data (), blur_radius);
1709 if (my_fabs (get_blur_radius (start.data ()) - blur_radius) > (coord_t)0.01)
1710 {
1711 printf ("Screen blur %f %f\n", get_blur_radius (start.data ()),
1712 blur_radius);
1713 abort ();
1714 }
1715 }
1716 if (optimize_scanner_mtf_sigma)
1717 {
1718 start[mtf_sigma_index] = 0;
1719 }
1720 if (optimize_scanner_mtf_defocus)
1721 {
1722 start[mtf_defocus_index] = 0;
1723 }
1724 if (optimize_scanner_mtf_channel_defocus)
1725 {
1726 start[mtf_defocus_index] = 0;
1727 start[mtf_defocus_index + 1] = 0;
1728 start[mtf_defocus_index + 2] = 0;
1729 }
1730 /* TODO: Maybe we want to use previous results and start from params by
1731 * default. */
1732 if (flags & finetune_use_strip_widths)
1733 {
1734 set_red_strip_width (start.data (), red_strip_width);
1735 set_green_strip_width (start.data (), green_strip_width);
1736 }
1737 /* Default Dufaycolor strip widths. */
1738 else if (type == Dufay)
1739 {
1740 set_red_strip_width (start.data (), dufaycolor::red_strip_width);
1741 set_green_strip_width (start.data (), dufaycolor::green_strip_width);
1742 }
1743 /* Dioptichromes seem to be printed with strips of equal widths. */
1744 else if (dufay_like_screen_p (type))
1745 {
1746 set_red_strip_width (start.data (), (coord_t)0.5);
1747 set_green_strip_width (start.data (), (coord_t)0.5);
1748 }
1749 /* Joly and Warner-Powrie should be approx 1/3 each. */
1750 else
1751 {
1752 set_red_strip_width (start.data (), (coord_t)1.0 / (coord_t)3);
1753 set_green_strip_width (start.data (), (coord_t)1.0 / (coord_t)3);
1754 }
1755 if (fog_index >= 0)
1756 {
1757 start[fog_index + 0] = 0;
1758 start[fog_index + 1] = 0;
1759 start[fog_index + 2] = 0;
1760 }
1761 if (mix_weights_index >= 0)
1762 {
1763 start[mix_weights_index + 0] = (coord_t)1.0 / (coord_t)3;
1764 start[mix_weights_index + 1] = (coord_t)1.0 / (coord_t)3;
1765 if (least_squares)
1766 start[mix_weights_index + 2] = (coord_t)1.0 / (coord_t)3;
1767 }
1768 if (mix_dark_index >= 0)
1769 start[mix_dark_index] = 0;
1770
1771 /* Verify that everything is set up. */
1772 if (colorscreen_checking)
1773 for (int i = 0; i < n_values; i++)
1774 assert (start[i] != INT_MAX);
1775
1776 /* Once values are set up, be sure they are in range. This should be NOOP
1777 most of time unless we get mad input. */
1778 constrain (start.data ());
1779
1780 /* Maxgray is used to normalize equations for least squares to reduce
1781 numeric errors. */
1782 maxgray = mingray = 0;
1783 if (!tiles[0].bw.empty ())
1784 {
1785 mingray = maxgray = bw_get_pixel (0, { 0, 0 });
1786 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
1787 for (int y = 0; y < theight; y++)
1788 for (int x = 0; x < twidth; x++)
1789 {
1790 maxgray = std::max (maxgray, bw_get_pixel (tileid, { x, y }));
1791 mingray = std::min (mingray, bw_get_pixel (tileid, { x, y }));
1792 }
1793 }
1794
1795 /* Fog should not be much greater than minimal value in the tile. */
1796 if (optimize_fog)
1797 {
1798 rgb_histogram hist;
1799 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
1800 for (int y = 0; y < theight; y++)
1801 for (int x = 0; x < twidth; x++)
1802 hist.pre_account (tiles[tileid].color[y * twidth + x]);
1803 hist.finalize_range (65535);
1804 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
1805 for (int y = 0; y < theight; y++)
1806 for (int x = 0; x < twidth; x++)
1807 hist.account (tiles[tileid].color[y * twidth + x]);
1808 hist.finalize ();
1809 fog_range = hist.find_min ((coord_t)0.1);
1810 if (!(fog_range.red > 0))
1811 fog_range.red = (luminosity_t)4 / (luminosity_t)65536;
1812 if (!(fog_range.green > 0))
1813 fog_range.green = (luminosity_t)4 / (luminosity_t)65536;
1814 if (!(fog_range.blue > 0))
1815 fog_range.blue = (luminosity_t)4 / (luminosity_t)65536;
1816 }
1817 else
1818 assert (!colorscreen_checking || fog_index == -1);
1819
1820 /* Normalize tile. This depends on fog, so with fog optimization
1821 we normalize later. */
1822 if (normalize && !optimize_fog)
1823 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
1824 for (int y = 0; y < theight; y++)
1825 for (int x = 0; x < twidth; x++)
1826 {
1827 rgbdata &c = tiles[tileid].color[y * twidth + x];
1828 luminosity_t sum = c.red + c.green + c.blue;
1829 if (sum > 0)
1830 c /= sum;
1831 }
1832
1833 if (least_squares)
1834 {
1835 free_least_squares ();
1836 alloc_least_squares ();
1837 if (!optimize_fog || fog_by_least_squares)
1838 init_least_squares (nullptr);
1839 }
1840 simulated_screen_border = 0;
1841 simulated_screen_width = twidth;
1842 simulated_screen_height = theight;
1843 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
1844 tiles[tileid].simulated_screen.resize (
1845 simulated_screen_width * simulated_screen_height);
1846 }
1847
1848 void
1849 compute_contrast ()
1850 {
1851 if (!tiles[0].bw.empty ())
1852 contrast = get_positional_color_contrast (type, last_color, finetune_coordinates == 2);
1853 else
1854 contrast = std::max ({get_positional_color_contrast (type, {(luminosity_t)last_red.red, (luminosity_t)last_green.red, (luminosity_t)last_blue.red}, finetune_coordinates == 2),
1855 get_positional_color_contrast (type, {(luminosity_t)last_red.green, (luminosity_t)last_green.green, (luminosity_t)last_blue.green}, finetune_coordinates == 2),
1856 get_positional_color_contrast (type, {(luminosity_t)last_red.blue, (luminosity_t)last_green.blue, (luminosity_t)last_blue.blue}, finetune_coordinates == 2)});
1857 }
1858
1859 /* Invoke solver. If REPORT is true, set progress report.
1860 PROGRESS is used to report progress.
1861 This may be disabled if we run in OpenMP parallel. */
1862 coord_t
1863 solve (progress_info *progress, bool report)
1864 {
1865 // if (verbose)
1866 // solver.print_values (solver.start);
1867 coord_t uncertainty = simplex<coord_t, finetune_solver> (
1868 *this, "finetuning", progress, report);
1869 compute_contrast ();
1870 if (contrast > 1 / (luminosity_t)65535)
1871 uncertainty = std::min (uncertainty / contrast, (coord_t)(10000000));
1872 else
1873 uncertainty = 100000000;
1874 free_least_squares ();
1875 return uncertainty;
1876 }
1877
1878 /* Get screen pixel for simulated screen TILE at point P. */
1879 rgbdata
1880 get_simulated_screen_pixel (int tile, int_point_t p)
1881 {
1882 return tiles[tile].simulated_screen[p.y * simulated_screen_width + p.x];
1883 }
1884
1885 /* Apply blur to SRC_SCR and compute DST_SCR.
1886 Values are in vector V. TILEID is the tile ID.
1887 If WEIGHT_SCR is non-null, use it as a weight screen. */
1888 void
1889 apply_blur (coord_t *v, int tileid, screen *dst_scr, screen *src_scr,
1890 screen *weight_scr = nullptr)
1891 {
1892 rgbdata blur = get_channel_blur_radius (v);
1893
1894 if (weight_scr)
1895 {
1896 rgbdata i = get_emulsion_intensities (v, tileid);
1897 point_t offset = get_emulsion_offset (v, tileid);
1898 if (offset.x == 0 && offset.y == 0)
1899 for (int y = 0; y < screen::size; y++)
1900 for (int x = 0; x < screen::size; x++)
1901 {
1902 luminosity_t w = weight_scr->mult[y][x][0] * i.red
1903 + weight_scr->mult[y][x][1] * i.green
1904 + weight_scr->mult[y][x][2] * i.blue;
1905 tiles[tileid].merged_scr->mult[y][x][0]
1906 = src_scr->mult[y][x][0] * w;
1907 tiles[tileid].merged_scr->mult[y][x][1]
1908 = src_scr->mult[y][x][1] * w;
1909 tiles[tileid].merged_scr->mult[y][x][2]
1910 = src_scr->mult[y][x][2] * w;
1911 }
1912 else
1913 for (int y = 0; y < screen::size; y++)
1914 for (int x = 0; x < screen::size; x++)
1915 {
1916 rgbdata wd = weight_scr->interpolated_mult (
1917 (point_t){ x * ((coord_t)1 / (coord_t)screen::size),
1918 y * ((coord_t)1 / (coord_t)screen::size) }
1919 + offset);
1920 luminosity_t w
1921 = wd.red * i.red + wd.green * i.green + wd.blue * i.blue;
1922 tiles[tileid].merged_scr->mult[y][x][0]
1923 = src_scr->mult[y][x][0] * w;
1924 tiles[tileid].merged_scr->mult[y][x][1]
1925 = src_scr->mult[y][x][1] * w;
1926 tiles[tileid].merged_scr->mult[y][x][2]
1927 = src_scr->mult[y][x][2] * w;
1928 }
1929 src_scr = tiles[tileid].merged_scr.get ();
1930 }
1931
1932 if ((optimize_scanner_mtf_sigma || optimize_scanner_mtf_defocus)
1933 || (!optimize_screen_blur && !optimize_screen_channel_blurs))
1934 {
1935 sharpen_parameters sp, sp_green, sp_blue;
1936 sharpen_parameters *vs[3] = { &sp, &sp, &sp };
1937 sp = render_sharpen_params;
1938 // sp.scanner_mtf = mtf_params;
1939 sp.scanner_mtf.sigma = get_scanner_mtf_sigma (v);
1940 sp.scanner_mtf_scale *= pixel_size;
1941 // sp.mode = sharpen_parameters::none;
1942 if (sp.scanner_mtf.simulate_diffraction_p ())
1943 {
1944 sp.scanner_mtf.defocus = get_scanner_mtf_defocus (v);
1945 if (!tiles[0].color.empty ())
1946 sp.scanner_mtf.wavelength = 550;
1947 if (/*tiles[0].color ||*/ optimize_scanner_mtf_channel_defocus)
1948 {
1949 vs[0] = &sp;
1950 sp_green = sp;
1951 vs[1] = &sp_green;
1952 sp_blue = sp;
1953 vs[2] = &sp_blue;
1954
1955 rgbdata defocus = get_scanner_mtf_channel_defocus (v);
1956 sp.scanner_mtf.defocus = defocus.red;
1957 sp_green.scanner_mtf.defocus = defocus.green;
1958 sp_blue.scanner_mtf.defocus = defocus.blue;
1959#if 0
1960 /* TODO: We should defocus only after applying scanner reaction to screen colors. */
1961 sp.scanner_mtf.wavelength = 466;
1962 sp_green.scanner_mtf.wavelength = 526;
1963 sp_blue.scanner_mtf.wavelength = 653;
1964#endif
1965 }
1966 }
1967 else
1968 {
1969 sp.scanner_mtf.blur_diameter = get_scanner_mtf_defocus (v);
1970 if (optimize_scanner_mtf_channel_defocus)
1971 {
1972 vs[0] = &sp;
1973 sp_green = sp;
1974 vs[1] = &sp_green;
1975 sp_blue = sp;
1976 vs[2] = &sp_blue;
1977 rgbdata blur_diameter = get_scanner_mtf_channel_defocus (v);
1978 sp.scanner_mtf.blur_diameter = blur_diameter.red;
1979 sp_green.scanner_mtf.blur_diameter = blur_diameter.green;
1980 sp_blue.scanner_mtf.blur_diameter = blur_diameter.blue;
1981 }
1982 }
1983 dst_scr->initialize_with_sharpen_parameters (*src_scr, vs,
1984 tile_sharpened, parallel);
1985 }
1986 else
1987 dst_scr->initialize_with_blur (*src_scr, blur * pixel_size);
1988 }
1989
1990 /* Initialize screen for tile TILEID using values in vector V.
1991 Return true if screen was updated. */
1992 bool
1993 init_screen (coord_t *v, int tileid)
1994 {
1995 luminosity_t emulsion_blur = get_emulsion_blur_radius (v);
1996 rgbdata blur = get_channel_blur_radius (v);
1997 luminosity_t scanner_mtf_sigma = get_scanner_mtf_sigma (v);
1998 rgbdata scanner_mtf_defocus = get_scanner_mtf_channel_defocus (v);
1999 luminosity_t red_strip_width = get_red_strip_width (v);
2000 luminosity_t green_strip_width = get_green_strip_width (v);
2001 rgbdata intensities = get_emulsion_intensities (v, tileid);
2002 point_t emulsion_offset = get_emulsion_offset (v, tileid);
2003 bool global_updated = false;
2004 if (red_strip_width != last_width || green_strip_width != last_height)
2005 {
2006 original_scr->initialize (type, red_strip_width, green_strip_width);
2007 last_width = red_strip_width;
2008 last_height = green_strip_width;
2009 global_updated = true;
2010 }
2011
2012 /* Fast path: If everything is fixed, use screen cache. We will not
2013 fill it with temporary screens then. */
2014 if (!optimize_scanner_mtf_sigma && !optimize_scanner_mtf_defocus
2015 && !optimize_scanner_mtf_channel_defocus
2016 && !optimize_screen_blur && !optimize_screen_channel_blurs
2017 && !optimize_strips && !optimize_emulsion_blur
2018 && !optimize_emulsion_intensities && !optimize_emulsion_offset)
2019 {
2020 if (global_updated)
2021 screen_revision++;
2022 if (tiles[tileid].last_screen_revision != screen_revision)
2023 {
2024 sharpen_parameters sp = render_sharpen_params;
2025 sp.scanner_mtf_scale *= pixel_size;
2026 std::shared_ptr <screen> scr = render_to_scr::get_screen (type, false,
2027 tile_sharpened,
2028 sp,
2029 red_strip_width,
2030 green_strip_width,
2031 NULL);
2032 memcpy (tiles[tileid].scr.get (), scr.get (), sizeof (screen));
2033 return true;
2034 }
2035 return false;
2036 }
2037
2038 if (optimize_emulsion_blur
2039 && (emulsion_blur != last_emulsion_blur || global_updated))
2040 {
2041 emulsion_scr->initialize_with_blur (*original_scr, emulsion_blur);
2042 last_emulsion_blur = emulsion_blur;
2043 global_updated = true;
2044 }
2045
2046 if (blur != last_blur || scanner_mtf_sigma != last_scanner_mtf_sigma
2047 || scanner_mtf_defocus != last_scanner_mtf_defocus)
2048 {
2049 last_blur = blur;
2050 last_scanner_mtf_sigma = scanner_mtf_sigma;
2051 last_scanner_mtf_defocus = scanner_mtf_defocus;
2052 global_updated = true;
2053 }
2054
2055 if (global_updated)
2056 screen_revision++;
2057
2058 if (tiles[tileid].last_screen_revision != screen_revision
2059 || tiles[tileid].last_emulsion_intensities != intensities
2060 || tiles[tileid].last_emulsion_offset != emulsion_offset)
2061 {
2062 apply_blur (v, tileid, tiles[tileid].scr.get (),
2063 optimize_emulsion_blur && !optimize_emulsion_intensities
2064 ? emulsion_scr.get ()
2065 : original_scr.get (),
2066 optimize_emulsion_intensities ? emulsion_scr.get ()
2067 : nullptr);
2068 tiles[tileid].last_screen_revision = screen_revision;
2069 tiles[tileid].last_emulsion_intensities = intensities;
2070 tiles[tileid].last_emulsion_offset = emulsion_offset;
2071 return true;
2072 }
2073 return false;
2074 }

2076 /* Evaluate screen pixel for TILEID at X,Y with offset OFF.
2077 Fast version that does not assume scaling/rotation. */
2078 pure_attr inline rgbdata
2079 evaluate_screen_pixel_fast (int tileid, int x, int y, point_t off) const
2080 {
2081 point_t p = tiles[tileid].pos[y * twidth + x] + off;
2082 /* When using scanner mtf, the screen is already blurred to
2083 estimate sensor mtf as well. No need for antialiasing
2084 then. */
2085 return tiles[tileid].scr->interpolated_mult (p);
2086 }
2087
2088 /* Evaluate screen pixel for TILEID at X,Y with offset OFF. */
2089 pure_attr inline rgbdata
2090 evaluate_screen_pixel_slow (coord_t *v, int tileid, int x, int y) const
2091 {
2092 point_t p = get_pos (v, tileid, {x, y});
2093 /* When using scanner mtf, the screen is already blurred to
2094 estimate sensor mtf as well. No need for antialiasing
2095 then. */
2096 return tiles[tileid].scr->interpolated_mult (p);
2097 }
2098
2099 /* Evaluate pixel at (X,Y) using RGB values RED, GREEN, BLUE and offsets OFF
2100 compensating coordinates stored in tile_pos.
2101 Values are in vector V. TILEID is the tile ID.
2102 MIX_WEIGHTS and MIX_DARK are used for infrared simulation. */
2103 pure_attr inline rgbdata
2104 evaluate_pixel (coord_t *v, int tileid, double_rgbdata red,
2105 double_rgbdata green, double_rgbdata blue, int x, int y,
2106 double_rgbdata mix_weights, double mix_dark)
2107 {
2108 rgbdata m = get_simulated_screen_pixel (tileid, { x, y });
2109 rgbdata c = ((red * m.red + green * m.green + blue * m.blue)
2110 * ((coord_t)1.0 / (coord_t)rgbscale));
2111 if (simulate_infrared)
2112 {
2113 rgbdata p = get_pixel (v, tileid, { x, y });
2114 luminosity_t intensity = p.red * mix_weights.red
2115 + p.green * mix_weights.green
2116 + p.blue * mix_weights.blue - mix_dark;
2117 c *= intensity;
2118 }
2119 return c;
2120 }
2121
2122 /* Simulate screen for TILEID using values in vector V.
2123 Return true if simulation was updated. */
2124 bool
2125 simulate_screen (coord_t *v, int tileid, bool force = false)
2126 {
2127 if (!optimize_coordinates)
2128 {
2129 point_t off = get_offset (v, tileid);
2130 if (!force && tiles[tileid].last_simulated_offset == off)
2131 return false;
2132 for (int y = 0; y < theight; y++)
2133 for (int x = 0; x < twidth; x++)
2134 tiles[tileid].simulated_screen[y * simulated_screen_width + x]
2135 = evaluate_screen_pixel_fast (tileid, x, y, off);
2136 tiles[tileid].last_simulated_offset = off;
2137 }
2138 else
2139 for (int y = 0; y < theight; y++)
2140 for (int x = 0; x < twidth; x++)
2141 tiles[tileid].simulated_screen[y * simulated_screen_width + x]
2142 = evaluate_screen_pixel_slow (v, tileid, x, y);
2143 return true;
2144 }

2149 bw_evaluate_pixel (int tileid, double_rgbdata color, int x, int y)
2150 {
2151 rgbdata m = get_simulated_screen_pixel (tileid, { x, y });

2153 + m.blue * color.blue) );

2161 if (normalize)

2164 if (ssum == 0)
2165 ssum = (luminosity_t)0.0000001;
2166 d /= ssum;
2167 }

2199 void
2200 determine_colors_using_data_collection (coord_t *v, double_rgbdata *ret_red,
2201 double_rgbdata *ret_green,
2202 double_rgbdata *ret_blue)
2203 {
2204 /* Use double_rgbdata to avoid accumulation of roundoff error. */
2205 double_rgbdata red = { 0, 0, 0 }, green = { 0, 0, 0 }, blue = { 0, 0, 0 };
2206 double_rgbdata color_red = { 0, 0, 0 }, color_green = { 0, 0, 0 },
2207 color_blue = { 0, 0, 0 };
2208 luminosity_t threshold = collection_threshold;
2209 /* Use double to avoid accumulation of roundoff error. */
2210 double wr = 0, wg = 0, wb = 0;
2211
2212 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
2213 for (int y = border; y < theight - border; y++)
2214 for (int x = border; x < twidth - border; x++)
2215 if (!noutliers || !tiles[tileid].outliers->test_bit (x, y))
2216 {
2217 rgbdata m = get_simulated_screen_pixel (tileid, { x, y });
2218 rgbdata d = get_pixel (v, tileid, { x, y });
2219 if (m.red > threshold)
2220 {
2221 coord_t val = m.red - threshold;
2222 wr += val;
2223 red += m * val;
2224 color_red += d * val;
2225 }
2226 if (m.green > threshold)
2227 {
2228 coord_t val = m.green - threshold;
2229 wg += val;
2230 green += m * val;
2231 color_green += d * val;
2232 }
2233 if (m.blue > threshold)
2234 {
2235 coord_t val = m.blue - threshold;
2236 wb += val;
2237 blue += m * val;
2238 color_blue += d * val;
2239 }
2240 }
2241 if (!wr || !wg || !wb)
2242 {
2243 *ret_red = *ret_green = *ret_blue = { -15, -15, -15 };
2244 return;
2245 }
2246
2247 red /= wr;
2248 green /= wg;
2249 blue /= wb;
2250 color_red /= wr;
2251 color_green /= wg;
2252 color_blue /= wb;
2253 // sum /= n;
2254 // sum.print (stdout);
2255 double_rgbdata cred = (double_rgbdata){ red.red, green.red, blue.red };
2256 double_rgbdata cgreen
2257 = (double_rgbdata){ red.green, green.green, blue.green };
2258 double_rgbdata cblue = (double_rgbdata){ red.blue, green.blue, blue.blue };
2259 matrix4x4<double> sat (cred.red, cgreen.red, cblue.red, 0, cred.green,
2260 cgreen.green, cblue.green, 0, cred.blue,
2261 cgreen.blue, cblue.blue, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1);
2262 sat = sat.invert ();
2263 // sat.apply_to_rgb (color.red / (2 * maxgray), color.green / (2 *
2264 // maxgray), color.blue / (2 * maxgray), &color.red, &color.green,
2265 // &color.blue);
2266 sat.apply_to_rgb (color_red.red, color_green.red, color_blue.red,
2267 &color_red.red, &color_green.red, &color_blue.red);
2268 sat.apply_to_rgb (color_red.green, color_green.green, color_blue.green,
2269 &color_red.green, &color_green.green, &color_blue.green);
2270 sat.apply_to_rgb (color_red.blue, color_green.blue, color_blue.blue,
2271 &color_red.blue, &color_green.blue, &color_blue.blue);
2272 /* Colors should be real reactions of scanner, so no negative values and
2273 also no excessively large values. Allow some overexposure. */
2274 for (int c = 0; c < 3; c++)
2275 {
2276 color_red[c] = std::clamp (color_red[c], (double)-0.01, (double)2);
2277 color_green[c] = std::clamp (color_green[c], (double)-0.01, (double)2);
2278 color_blue[c] = std::clamp (color_blue[c], (double)-0.01, (double)2);
2279 }
2280
2281 *ret_red = color_red;
2282 *ret_green = color_green;
2283 *ret_blue = color_blue;
2284 }
2285
2286 coord_t
2287 determine_colors_using_least_squares (coord_t *v, double_rgbdata *red,
2288 double_rgbdata *green,
2289 double_rgbdata *blue)
2290 {
2291 /* Use double to not accumulate errors. */
2292 double sqsum = 0;
2293
2294 if (!least_squares_initialized)
2295 abort ();
2296
2297 int e = 0;
2298 if (simulate_infrared)
2299 {
2300 rgbdata mix_weights = get_mix_weights (v);
2301 luminosity_t mix_dark = get_mix_dark (v);
2302 luminosity_t sum = /*v[mix_weights_index + 3]*/ 1;
2303
2304 /* See below. */
2305 assert (!fog_by_least_squares);
2306 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
2307 for (int y = border; y < theight - border; y++)
2308 for (int x = border; x < twidth - border; x++)
2309 if (!noutliers || !tiles[tileid].outliers->test_bit (x, y))
2310 {
2311 rgbdata c = get_simulated_screen_pixel (tileid, { x, y });
2312 rgbdata d = fog_by_least_squares
2313 ? get_pixel_nofog (tileid, { x, y })
2314 : get_pixel (v, tileid, { x, y });
2315 /* ??? This is not right when fog is optimized by least
2316 squares. For this reason we use non-linear solver to
2317 optimize fog. */
2318 c *= d.red * mix_weights.red + d.green * mix_weights.green
2319 + d.blue * mix_weights.blue - mix_dark;
2320 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 0, c.red); /* red.red */
2321 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 1, c.green); /* green.red */
2322 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 2, c.blue); /* blue.red */
2323 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 3, 0); /* red.green */
2324 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 4, 0); /* green.green */
2325 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 5, 0); /* blue.green */
2326 if (fog_by_least_squares)
2327 {
2328 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 6, 1);
2329 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 7, 0);
2330 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 8, 0);
2331 }
2332 gsl_vector_set (gsl_y[0].get (), e, d.red);
2333 e++;
2334 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 0, 0); /* red.red */
2335 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 1, 0); /* green.red */
2336 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 2, 0); /* blue.red */
2337 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 3, c.red); /* red.green */
2338 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 4, c.green); /* green.green */
2339 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 5, c.blue); /* blue.green */
2340 if (fog_by_least_squares)
2341 {
2342 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 6, 0);
2343 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 7, 1);
2344 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 8, 0);
2345 }
2346 gsl_vector_set (gsl_y[0].get (), e, d.green);
2347 e++;
2348
2349 /* red.red * mix_weights.red + red.green * mix_weights.green
2350 + red.blue * mix_weights.blue = sum gives: red.blue = (sum
2351 - red.red * mix_weights.red - red.green *
2352 mix_weights.green) / mix_weights.blue
2353
2354 Analogously:
2355 green.blue = (sum - green.red * mix_weights.red -
2356 green.green * mix_weights.green) / mix_weights.blue
2357 blue.blue = (sum - blue.red * mix_weights.red - blue.green
2358 * mix_weights.green) / mix_weights.blue */
2359
2360 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 0,
2361 -c.red
2362 * (mix_weights.red
2363 / mix_weights.blue)); /* red.red */
2364 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 1,
2365 -c.green
2366 * (mix_weights.red
2367 / mix_weights.blue)); /* green.red */
2368 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 2,
2369 -c.blue
2370 * (mix_weights.red
2371 / mix_weights.blue)); /* blue.red */
2372 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 3,
2373 -c.red
2374 * (mix_weights.green
2375 / mix_weights.blue)); /* red.green */
2376 gsl_matrix_set (
2377 gsl_X.get (), e, 4,
2378 -c.green
2379 * (mix_weights.green
2380 / mix_weights.blue)); /* green.green */
2381 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 5,
2382 -c.blue
2383 * (mix_weights.green
2384 / mix_weights.blue)); /* blue.green */
2385 if (fog_by_least_squares)
2386 {
2387 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 6, 0);
2388 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 7, 0);
2389 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 8, 1);
2390 }
2391 gsl_vector_set (gsl_y[0].get (), e,
2392 d.blue
2393 - sum * (c.red + c.green + c.blue)
2394 / mix_weights.blue);
2395 e++;
2396 }
2397 if (fog_by_least_squares)
2398 {
2399 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 0, 0);
2400 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 1, 0);
2401 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 2, 0);
2402 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 3, 0);
2403 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 4, 0);
2404 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 5, 0);
2405 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 6,
2406 sample_points () * ((double)4 / 65546));
2407 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 7, 0);
2408 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 8, 0);
2409 gsl_vector_set (gsl_y[0].get (), e, 0);
2410 e++;
2411 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 0, 0);
2412 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 1, 0);
2413 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 2, 0);
2414 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 3, 0);
2415 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 4, 0);
2416 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 5, 0);
2417 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 6, 0);
2418 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 7,
2419 sample_points () * ((double)4 / 65546));
2420 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 8, 0);
2421 gsl_vector_set (gsl_y[0].get (), e, 0);
2422 e++;
2423 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 0, 0);
2424 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 1, 0);
2425 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 2, 0);
2426 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 3, 0);
2427 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 4, 0);
2428 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 5, 0);
2429 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 6, 0);
2430 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 7, 0);
2431 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 8,
2432 sample_points () * ((double)4 / 65546));
2433 gsl_vector_set (gsl_y[0].get (), e, 0);
2434 e++;
2435 }
2436 double chisq;
2437 if (gsl_multifit_linear (gsl_X.get (), gsl_y[0].get (), gsl_c.get (), gsl_cov.get (), &chisq,
2438 gsl_work.get ()) != GSL_SUCCESS)
2439 return 1e10;
2440 /* Colors should be real reactions of scanner, so no negative values
2441 and also no excessively large values. Allow some overexposure. */
2442 (*red).red = gsl_vector_get (gsl_c.get (), 0);
2443 // to_range ((*red).red, -0.2, 2);
2444 (*green).red = gsl_vector_get (gsl_c.get (), 1);
2445 // to_range ((*green).red, -0.2, 2);
2446 (*blue).red = gsl_vector_get (gsl_c.get (), 2);
2447 // to_range ((*blue).red, -0.2, 2);
2448
2449 (*red).green = gsl_vector_get (gsl_c.get (), 3);
2450 // to_range ((*red).green, -0.2, 2);
2451 (*green).green = gsl_vector_get (gsl_c.get (), 4);
2452 // to_range ((*green).green, -0.2, 2);
2453 (*blue).green = gsl_vector_get (gsl_c.get (), 5);
2454 // to_range ((*blue).green, -0.2, 2);
2455
2456 (*red).blue = (sum - (*red).red * mix_weights.red
2457 - (*red).green * mix_weights.green)
2458 / mix_weights.blue;
2459 // to_range ((*red).blue, 0, 2);
2460 (*green).blue = (sum - (*green).red * mix_weights.red
2461 - (*green).green * mix_weights.green)
2462 / mix_weights.blue;
2463 // to_range ((*green).blue, 0, 2);
2464 (*blue).blue = (sum - (*blue).red * mix_weights.red
2465 - (*blue).green * mix_weights.green)
2466 / mix_weights.blue;
2467 // to_range ((*blue).blue, 0, 2);
2468
2469 if (fog_by_least_squares)
2470 {
2471 last_fog.red = std::clamp ((luminosity_t)gsl_vector_get (gsl_c.get (), 6),
2472 /*-fog_range.red*/ (luminosity_t)-0.1,
2473 fog_range.red);
2474 last_fog.green = std::clamp (
2475 (luminosity_t)gsl_vector_get (gsl_c.get (), 7),
2476 /*-fog_range.green*/ (luminosity_t)-0.1, fog_range.green);
2477 last_fog.blue = std::clamp (
2478 (luminosity_t)gsl_vector_get (gsl_c.get (), 8),
2479 /*-fog_range.blue*/ (luminosity_t)-0.1, fog_range.blue);
2480 }
2481 return chisq;
2482 }
2483 else
2484 {
2485 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
2486 for (int y = border; y < theight - border; y++)
2487 for (int x = border; x < twidth - border; x++)
2488 if (!noutliers || !tiles[tileid].outliers->test_bit (x, y))
2489 {
2490 rgbdata c = get_simulated_screen_pixel (tileid, { x, y });
2491 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 0, c.red);
2492 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 1, c.green);
2493 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 2, c.blue);
2494 if (fog_by_least_squares)
2495 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 3, 1);
2496 e++;
2497 }
2498 if (fog_by_least_squares)
2499 {
2500 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 0, 0);
2501 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 1, 0);
2502 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 2, 0);
2503 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 3,
2504 sample_points () * ((double)4 / 65546));
2505 e++;
2506 }
2507 if (e != (int)gsl_X->size1)
2508 abort ();
2509 for (int ch = 0; ch < 3; ch++)
2510 {
2511 double chisq;
2512 if (gsl_multifit_linear (gsl_X.get (), gsl_y[ch].get (), gsl_c.get (), gsl_cov.get (), &chisq,
2513 gsl_work.get ()) != GSL_SUCCESS)
2514 return 1e10;
2515 sqsum += chisq;
2516 /* Colors should be real reactions of scanner, so no negative
2517 values and also no excessively large values. Allow some
2518 overexposure. */
2519 (*red)[ch] = std::clamp ((luminosity_t)gsl_vector_get (gsl_c.get (), 0),
2520 (luminosity_t)0, (luminosity_t)2);
2521 (*green)[ch] = std::clamp ((luminosity_t)gsl_vector_get (gsl_c.get (), 1),
2522 (luminosity_t)0, (luminosity_t)2);
2523 (*blue)[ch] = std::clamp ((luminosity_t)gsl_vector_get (gsl_c.get (), 2),
2524 (luminosity_t)0, (luminosity_t)2);
2525 if (fog_by_least_squares)
2526 {
2527 last_fog[ch]
2528 = std::clamp ((luminosity_t)gsl_vector_get (gsl_c.get (), 3),
2529 (luminosity_t)-0.1, fog_range[ch]);
2530 }
2531 }
2532 return sqsum;
2533 }
2534 }

2536 rgbdata
2537 bw_determine_color_using_data_collection (coord_t *v)
2538 {
2539 /* Use double_rgbdata to avoid accumulation of roundoff error. */
2540 double_rgbdata red = { 0, 0, 0 }, green = { 0, 0, 0 }, blue = { 0, 0, 0 };
2541 double_rgbdata color = { 0, 0, 0 };
2542 luminosity_t threshold = collection_threshold;
2543 /* Use double to avoid accumulation of roundoff error. */
2544 double wr = 0, wg = 0, wb = 0;
2545
2546 /* This follows same algorithm as data collection in analyze_base.
2547 We collect data only if screen has intensity greater than zero
2548 in given channel. We also make statistics on how much saturation
2549 this process can lose and reverts that. */
2550 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
2551 for (int y = border; y < theight - border; y++)
2552 for (int x = border; x < twidth - border; x++)
2553 if (!noutliers || !tiles[tileid].outliers->test_bit (x, y))
2554 {
2555 rgbdata m = get_simulated_screen_pixel (tileid, { x, y });
2556 luminosity_t l = bw_get_pixel (tileid, { x, y });
2557 if (m.red > threshold)
2558 {
2559 coord_t val = m.red - threshold;
2560 wr += val;
2561 red += m * val;
2562 color.red += l * val;
2563 }
2564 if (m.green > threshold)
2565 {
2566 coord_t val = m.green - threshold;
2567 wg += val;
2568 green += m * val;
2569 color.green += l * val;
2570 }
2571 if (m.blue > threshold)
2572 {
2573 coord_t val = m.blue - threshold;
2574 wb += val;
2575 blue += m * val;
2576 color.blue += l * val;
2577 }
2578 }
2579 if (!(wr > 0) || !(wg > 0) || !(wb > 0))
2580 return { -10, -10, -10 };
2581
2582 red /= wr;
2583 green /= wg;
2584 blue /= wb;
2585 color.red /= wr;
2586 color.green /= wg;
2587 color.blue /= wb;
2588
2589 double_rgbdata cred = (double_rgbdata){ red.red, green.red, blue.red };
2590 double_rgbdata cgreen
2591 = (double_rgbdata){ red.green, green.green, blue.green };
2592 double_rgbdata cblue = (double_rgbdata){ red.blue, green.blue, blue.blue };
2593 matrix4x4<double> sat (cred.red, cgreen.red, cblue.red, 0, cred.green,
2594 cgreen.green, cblue.green, 0, cred.blue,
2595 cgreen.blue, cblue.blue, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1);
2596 sat = sat.invert ();
2597 sat.apply_to_rgb (color.red, color.green, color.blue, &color.red,
2598 &color.green, &color.blue);
2599 /* If infrared channel is simulated, negative values may be possible
2600 and it is kind of hard to constrain to reasonable bounds.
2601 Still allow values somewhat out of range to account for possible
2602 over-exposure or cropping */
2603 if (!bw_is_simulated_infrared)
2604 {
2605 color.red = std::clamp (color.red, (double)-0.1, (double)1.1);
2606 color.green = std::clamp (color.green, (double)-0.1, (double)1.1);
2607 color.blue = std::clamp (color.blue, (double)-0.1, (double)1.1);
2608 }
2609 return color;
2610 }

2612 rgbdata
2613 bw_determine_color_using_least_squares (coord_t *v)
2614 {
2615 int e = 0;
2616 if (!least_squares_initialized)
2617 abort ();
2618 for (int tileid = 0; tileid < n_tiles; tileid++)
2619 for (int y = border; y < theight - border; y++)
2620 for (int x = border; x < twidth - border; x++)
2621 if (!noutliers || !tiles[tileid].outliers->test_bit (x, y))
2622 {
2623 rgbdata c = get_simulated_screen_pixel (tileid, { x, y });
2624 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 0, c.red);
2625 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 1, c.green);
2626 gsl_matrix_set (gsl_X.get (), e, 2, c.blue);
2627 e++;
2628 // gsl_vector_set (gsl_y[0], e, bw_get_pixel (x, y) / (2 *
2629 // maxgray));
2630 }
2631 if (e != (int)gsl_X->size1)
2632 abort ();
2633 double chisq;
2634 if (gsl_multifit_linear (gsl_X.get (), gsl_y[0].get (), gsl_c.get (),
2635 gsl_cov.get (), &chisq, gsl_work.get ()) != GSL_SUCCESS)
2636 return { -1, -1, -1 };
2637 rgbdata color
2638 = { (luminosity_t)gsl_vector_get (gsl_c.get (), 0) * (2 * maxgray),
2639 (luminosity_t)gsl_vector_get (gsl_c.get (), 1) * (2 * maxgray),
2640 (luminosity_t)gsl_vector_get (gsl_c.get (), 2) * (2 * maxgray) };
2641 /* If infrared channel is simulated, negative values may be possible
2642 and it is kind of hard to constrain to reasonable bounds.
2643 Still allow values somewhat out of range to account for possible
2644 over-exposure or cropping */
2645 if (!bw_is_simulated_infrared)
2646 {
2647 color.red
2648 = std::clamp (color.red, (luminosity_t)-0.1, (luminosity_t)1.1);
2649 color.green
2650 = std::clamp (color.green, (luminosity_t)-0.1, (luminosity_t)1.1);
2651 color.blue
2652 = std::clamp (color.blue, (luminosity_t)-0.1, (luminosity_t)1.1);
2653 }
2654 return color;
2655 }

2657 rgbdata
2658 get_fog (coord_t *v)
2659 {
2660 if (!optimize_fog)
2661 return { 0, 0, 0 };
2662 if (fog_by_least_squares)
2663 return last_fog;
2664 assert (!colorscreen_checking || fog_index >= 0);
2665 return { (luminosity_t)v[fog_index] * fog_range.red,
2666 (luminosity_t)v[fog_index + 1] * fog_range.green,
2667 (luminosity_t)v[fog_index + 2] * fog_range.blue };

2670 rgbdata
2671 get_emulsion_intensities (coord_t *v, int tileid)
2672 {
2673 if (optimize_emulsion_intensities)
2674 {
2675 /* Together with screen colors these are defined only up to scaling
2676 * factor. */
2677 if (!tileid)
2678 {
2679 luminosity_t red = v[emulsion_intensity_index];
2680 luminosity_t green = v[emulsion_intensity_index + 1];
2681 luminosity_t blue = 1 - red - green;
2682 if (blue < 0)
2683 blue = 0;
2684 return { red, green, blue };
2685 }
2686 return { (luminosity_t)v[emulsion_intensity_index + 3 * tileid - 1],
2687 (luminosity_t)v[emulsion_intensity_index + 3 * tileid - 0],
2688 (luminosity_t)v[emulsion_intensity_index + 3 * tileid + 1] };
2689 }
2690 else
2691 return { 1, 1, 1 };

2695 get_sharpen_radius (coord_t *v)

2699 return 0;
2700 }
2701 coord_t
2702 get_sharpen_amount (coord_t *v)

2709 rgbdata
2710 get_mix_weights (coord_t *v)
2711 {
2712 if (mix_weights_index >= 0)
2713 {
2714 if (!least_squares)
2715 return { (luminosity_t)v[mix_weights_index],
2716 (luminosity_t)v[mix_weights_index + 1],
2717 1 - (luminosity_t)v[mix_weights_index]
2718 - (luminosity_t)v[mix_weights_index + 1] };
2719 else
2720 return { (luminosity_t)v[mix_weights_index],
2721 (luminosity_t)v[mix_weights_index + 1],
2722 (luminosity_t)v[mix_weights_index + 2] };
2723 }
2724 double_rgbdata red, green, blue;
2725 get_colors (v, &red, &green, &blue);
2726 color_matrix process_colors (red.red, red.green, red.blue, 0, green.red,
2727 green.green, green.blue, 0, blue.red,
2728 blue.green, blue.blue, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1);
2729 rgbdata ret;
2730 process_colors.invert ().apply_to_rgb (1, 1, 1, &ret.red, &ret.green,
2731 &ret.blue);
2732
2733#if 0
2734 if (simulate_infrared)
2735 return ret;
2736#endif
2737 luminosity_t sum = ret.red + ret.green + ret.blue;
2738 return ret * ((coord_t)1.0 / (coord_t)sum);
2739 }

2749 double_rgbdata
2750 bw_get_color (coord_t *v)
2751 {
2752 if (!least_squares && !data_collection)
2753 last_color = { v[color_index], v[color_index + 1], v[color_index + 2] };
2754 if (data_collection)
2755 last_color = bw_determine_color_using_data_collection (v);
2756 else
2757 last_color = bw_determine_color_using_least_squares (v);
2758 return last_color;
2759 }
2760 void
2761 get_colors (coord_t *v, double_rgbdata *red, double_rgbdata *green,
2762 double_rgbdata *blue)
2763 {
2764 if (!least_squares && !data_collection)
2765 {
2766 *red = { v[color_index], v[color_index + 1], v[color_index + 2] };
2767 *green
2768 = { v[color_index + 3], v[color_index + 4], v[color_index + 5] };
2769 *blue = { v[color_index + 6], v[color_index + 7], v[color_index + 8] };
2770 }
2771 else if (data_collection)
2772 determine_colors_using_data_collection (v, red, green, blue);
2773 else
2774 {
2775 if (least_squares && (optimize_fog && !fog_by_least_squares))
2776 init_least_squares (v);
2777 determine_colors_using_least_squares (v, red, green, blue);
2778 }
2779 last_red = *red;
2780 last_green = *green;
2781 last_blue = *blue;
2782 }
